title: What Is the Role of the Book of Mormon?
focus: Practice topic: inviting someone to read and pray about the Book of Mormon
intro: The Book of Mormon is another witness of Jesus Christ and the proof of the Restoration through Joseph Smith. In this lesson learners see its role, its help in answering the questions of the soul, and how to invite others to read it and pray.
preparation: Study 1 Nephi 10:14, 2 Nephi 3:12, 3 Nephi 16:4–5 and 3 Nephi 20:13. Bring a copy of the Book of Mormon for the class to hold. Think of one personal experience with the book you can share. Pray for each learner by name.

sections.title: A book that testifies of Christ
paras: Hold up the Book of Mormon. Ask: If you knew nothing about this book, what would you expect to find inside? Then read the title page together and ask what its writers wanted to convince the world of.

Ask: How does the Book of Mormon serve as a witness of Jesus Christ? How has it strengthened your testimony of Him? Let learners share with a partner. Remind them that daily reading is one of the best things they can do before entering the missionary training center.

sections.title: Two witnesses
paras: Read 2 Nephi 3:12 and then Ezekiel 37:15–17. The Lord promised that the record of Judah and the record of Joseph would grow together. Ask how these passages support the idea of two witnesses, and what blessing comes when the two books are used together.
Read 2 Corinthians 13:1 and Ephesians 4:5. Ask: What is the value of having two scriptural witnesses of Jesus Christ? Why should missionaries use both books when they help others learn?

sections.title: Gathering God’s children
paras: Let learners each read one of these: 1 Nephi 10:14, 3 Nephi 16:4–5 or 3 Nephi 20:13. They look for how God’s children are gathered. Draw out the truth that the Book of Mormon helps gather people to Christ.
Ask: How do missionaries take part in this gathering? Why must they use the Book of Mormon as they help others come to Christ?

sections.title: Conversion and the questions of the soul
paras: Read how Parley P. Pratt felt when he first read the Book of Mormon: he read with eagerness and felt the Spirit so strongly that he could hardly stop. Ask what the Spirit did for him and whether the learners have felt the Spirit as they read a passage.

Explain that every person has questions of the soul, such as: Who am I? Why am I here? Where am I going? Ask learners how they would use the Book of Mormon to find answers to these, and how a missionary can help someone else do the same.

sections.title: A foundation of testimony
paras: Ask: Why is the Book of Mormon called the keystone of our testimony? Why does the adversary oppose it? Missionaries do not argue about the book. They teach it, testify of it and invite people to read and pray to find out for themselves (see Moroni 10:4–5).

Explain that when a person has doubts, the best answer is often to read the book. Ask how the truth of the Book of Mormon confirms that Joseph Smith was a prophet, and how it has strengthened learners’ own testimonies of the Restoration.

steps.why: Teach the idea and why it matters for a missionary.

examples.title: Show the role of the Book of Mormon
examples.text: Write three words on the board: witness, gather, foundation. Use the title page, 3 Nephi 20:13 and Moroni 10:4–5 to show how the book testifies of Christ, gathers people to Him and builds testimony.

examples.title: Show two witnesses
examples.text: Hold up the Bible and the Book of Mormon. Read 2 Corinthians 13:1 and explain why two witnesses make a stronger case than one.

examples.title: Name the questions of the soul
examples.text: Write three questions of the soul on the board. Ask which could be answered by a passage from the Book of Mormon.

steps.why: Show one example of what learners will do.

examples.title: Introduce the book in two minutes
examples.text: Hold the book and say what it is, what it teaches about Christ and how it has blessed you. Then invite one learner to read Moroni 10:4–5 and pray.

examples.title: Show how to invite someone to read
examples.text: Show how to set a specific passage and a specific time, for example 3 Nephi 11 tonight. Then plan a follow-up.

examples.title: Share your own experience
examples.text: Tell a brief experience with the book. Show how to end with a simple testimony.

steps.why: Learners practise in pairs or small groups.

examples.title: Invite in pairs
examples.text: Each learner picks a passage, explains why it matters and invites a partner to read and pray. The partner plays a friend with a question.

examples.title: Answer a question of the soul
examples.text: In pairs, one asks a question of the soul. The other chooses a passage and shares what it teaches.

examples.title: Plan a real invitation
examples.text: Each learner writes the name of one person to give the Book of Mormon to this week, and how they will ask.

steps.why: Name what went well and what can improve.

examples.title: Partner feedback
examples.text: The learner who was taught says what was clearest and what felt most sincere. The teacher writes one thing to keep and one to improve.

examples.title: Three questions
examples.text: Ask: What went well? What would you change? What helped the listener most to understand the role of the Book of Mormon? Begin with the good.

examples.title: Simple checklist
examples.text: Was it simple? Was a scripture used and explained? Was the listener invited to act? Did the teacher speak with sincerity?

steps.why: Practise again with what was learned.

examples.title: Switch roles
examples.text: The learner who listened now teaches. Leave time for feedback both ways, then ask a few to share what they learned.

examples.title: Improve one thing
examples.text: Each learner teaches again and changes one thing from the feedback: a clearer sentence, a better scripture or a warmer invitation.

examples.title: Teach a new partner
examples.text: Find a new partner. Teach the same lesson again in a few minutes. Share one insight with the class.

testimony: Testify that the Book of Mormon is the word of God. Invite learners to share what it has done for them.

tips.text: Give learners a question to look for before a reading, a video or a quote.
Let learners practise a skill, then give feedback.
Ask for personal experiences, gently, with the right to pass.
Hold up a real copy of the Book of Mormon to start the discussion.

study: Read Moroni 10:4–5 together and ask what a person must do to know that the Book of Mormon is true.
invitations: Read the entire Book of Mormon and pray to know that it is true, if you have not already.
Make a habit of reading from the Book of Mormon every day.
Introduce someone to the Book of Mormon this week, in person or online, and invite them to read and pray.
